$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},
$$

where $\Phi(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $\mathbf{c}$ is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix $\Phi_0(t)$ of the system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14071035/assets/716aafac0120d14538c3cb2cea689450e9655f0d94147b04c0903c3bb5cde753.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={Φ}_{0}(t)\,c \\  & ={e}^{At}\,c \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} & t{e}^{-7t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-7t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{-7t} \\ {e}^{-7t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-7t},\end{aligned}
$$

where $c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.$
